title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Java seen properly, and four new things to find
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.41.0 makes every navigation feature see Java code that uses Kotlin, and adds four checks that report what the compiler cannot: events nobody listens to, enum entries nothing names, Remote Config keys nothing reads, and names declared twice that nothing mentions.

highlights.title: Find Usages Crosses the Line
highlights.description: Java files that use a Kotlin symbol were skipped before being searched, because the Java parser never reported their imports. On a project with 1731 Java files, a class imported by 58 of them returned none. It now returns all 58.

highlights.title: Events Nobody Listens To
highlights.description: Reports an event posted on a bus that nothing subscribes to. This one finds a missing behaviour rather than dead weight: someone wrote the trigger and the receiver went away. The bus is learned from register call sites, so Otto, greenrobot and a house-built bus all work.

highlights.title: Enum Entries and Remote Config Keys
highlights.description: Two more things the build never complains about: an enum variant nothing names, and a Remote Config default no line of the project reads. Measured on a 6410 file project, 36 entries and 29 keys, each confirmed by hand.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Fixes Find Usages, Find References, Call Hierarchy and the usage counter missing every Java file that uses a Kotlin symbol.
Fixes Rename corrupting Java files, and teaches it to rename Foo.java alongside the class it declares.
Fixes live sealed classes being reported as unreferenced when only their variants are imported.
Stops @Suppress from being read as a framework annotation, and stops @file:Suppress("UNUSED_PARAMETER") from silencing three unrelated checks.
Never reports anything inside a file whose header says a generator wrote it.
